messages.subject: P1-P4 in iteminfo (type = 'info')
parts:
Is there a way to find what P1-P4 refer to in item information curve, for an item from 0-3 (4-point Likert scale)? I searched the mirt R manual but cannot find this information. I know P1-P4 represent item thresholds, but I do not know whether mirt counts the thresholds from 0 to 4, or from 4 to 0.

The analysis summary is as follow. The item difficulty is negative for Question 1,2,4,6,7. Thanks for your help!

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: Re: P1-P4 in iteminfo (type = 'info')
parts:
I am not sure what it exactly is you want to know. The graph shows that for instance someone with an average latent trait level (theta = 0) has about .7 probability of endorsing the second respons category on item 1 (green curve). Where the lines crosses, the probability of another response increases. For instance it looks like that for someone with a latent trait level of 2 or above the probability of choosing the 4th response category is more likely as the curve of the 3th response category crosses below the curve of the 4th category at that point. I think MIRT counts the way your questions are keyed, i.e. from 0-4; higher score reflecting higher trait levels (if your questions are keyed this way)

Hope this helps

G.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: P1-P4 in iteminfo (type = 'info')
parts:
P1-P4 don't represent thresholds, these are the expected probability tracelines implied by your select IRT model for the item, and are associated with the respective categories in your item (P1 with the lowest category, while P4 would be the highest). Hence, they aren't information curves either. And the output you're printing is not demonstrating thresholds, but rather standardized factor loadings (if you want the actually parameters, use coef()). 

Phil

messages.subject: Re: P1-P4 in iteminfo (type = 'info')
parts:
I hope that this is the right group to ask this question. Kindly inform me of the right group if my question is not appropriate here. This question is about the interpretation of IRT results rather than MIRT software in particular.

Intuitively, I thought that expected probably of endorsement for a particular category would be conceptually similar to (and associated with) the measurement accuracy for that particular category. If the expected probability is high for a particular category (within a specific theta range), then the items would be more sensitive (and thus providing more information) in measuring participants (within a specific theta range). I am fairly new in IRT, however, and thus my understanding of IRT can be naive.

Examples in the item trace lines:

For the items on the first row, the P3 (green) peaks are noticeably higher than the P2 (pink) peaks. Can I conclude that these items are particularly suitable (i.e., more sensitive) to measurement of people below average (around theta = -1 to +0.5) than people above average?  My hypothesis is that these items are more suitable for measuring participants at the relatively lower end of the trait.

Again, for items on the second row,  the P3 (green) peaks are noticeably higher than the P2 (pink) peaks.  Can I conclude that these items are particularly suitable (i.e., more sensitive) to measurement of people above average (around theta = 0 to +1.5) than people below average? My hypothesis is that these items are more suitable for measuring participants at the relatively higher end of the trait.


If my understanding is correct, then the item information curves below do not make sense to me. Items on the first row do not seem particularly good (i.e., provide more information?) in measuring people at the lower end of the trait (than people  at the higher end of the trait  ), and items on the second row do not seem particularly good (i.e.,  provide more information?) in measuring people  at the higher end of the trait  (than people at the lower end of the trait). The 'categories' all have the same peak.


Thanks again for your help!

Chester

messages.author: 9403604069d4685f
messages.subject: Re: P1-P4 in iteminfo (type = 'info')
parts: I don't think that the probability of endorsing a specific category is the same construct as the amount of information obtained. Information should be conceptually related to reliability and not to the result on the item. Furthermore, I think that the plots in the output show the information of the whole item, and not just specific categories.
